DMA input bytes are minimal: B contributes exactly 10 distinct 16x16 tiles (2 k-chunks x 5 n-blocks), each loaded once = 2560 bytes; A has only 2 distinct tiles but the 32-row scratchpad fits just two 16-row tiles, so a B tile always occupies one slot and an A tile the other. Since only 2 accumulator tiles (32 rows) exist, at most two k=0 partial sums can be live, so one A0 load can serve at most 2 chunk-0 computes before A1 must be loaded for their chunk-1 accumulates; hence ceil(5/2)=3 loads each of A0 and A1 = 6 A tiles = 1536 bytes. Total 16 mvins x 256 = 4096 bytes, provably minimal. Command count is also minimal at 46: 10 computes (2 per n-block, mandatory for K=32) each require exactly one preload (10), 5 mvouts cover C (16x80 = 5 tiles, cols/rows fixed at 16), 16 mvins, 4 configs (config_ex must precede compute, config_st must precede mvout, both DMA streams configured), and 1 final fence. Structure: loop p over N//32 pairs blocks a=2p, b=2p+1; per pair the order is c0a, c0b (A0 at spad 0 resident, B tiles streamed to spad 16, overwrite into acc rows 0-15 and 16-31 via out_addr 0xA0000000/0xA0000010), then A1 loaded, then c1a, c1b (accumulate via out_addr 0xE0000000/0xE0000010), then both accumulator tiles drained with mvout to C offsets 32p and 32p+16 (row stride 320 bytes). Per-block K order (chunk 0 overwrite, chunk 1 accumulate) satisfies the ordered-reduction contract; every compute is immediately preceded by its own preload with accumulated=false and bd_spad_addr=4294967295; all scratchpad/accumulator starts are multiples of 16 within the 32-row capacities; block 4 is handled flat after the loop. Each compute uses the B tile staged by the immediately preceding preload, and the two accumulator tiles keep paired blocks independent."}
